title: Is my workflow already outdated? How is your workflow at the moment?
author: FutureLynx_
selftext:
im making my game using OpenCode + Deepseek 4.1. I made games in the past in JS, TS, C++ Unreal Engine, Godot. So if it's necessary I can also dive in the code.

But sometimes I feel like, damn, this feels too easy compared to what I used to have to do. What if im still missing out on something that could even make things better and faster. You know what i mean?

Particularly, in recent times I'm seeing a lot of projects from you guys that seem to be done only with Astra or Claude. It seems you make it using Blender MCP and do also the meshes. Its mind blogging. 

Though in my case im doing a 2D game isometric. And im using google flow to generate the sprites in all directions. This is the part that I think i'm wasting quite some time. I need sprites in all directions, and they need to make sense, then I need to download them, crop them and remove the background, and make sure they look good. This is the bare minimum. Then certain units have death animations, but most of my units dont have fancy animations. But since they are generated sprites I dont know any other way to make them so that they look perfectly isometric, and without mistakes, without requiring my supervision and treatment.

So yeah, I wonder if im doing it right or if my workflow is already obsolete. The good thing is that I'm not spending any money on this. Because I use only free tiers, and if I run out of stuff I just wait for the next days, or I just work on the code myself.

Let me know if my workflow is already outdated and if there is a better way of doing things...

comments.author: MorbilyABeast
comments.body:
Hit me with your deepseek workflow. Lost claude access. Was using claude code on desktop.

My workflow was simple. I had a dedicated chat pointed to my c++ files for my ue5 project. 

Id just iterate a new mechanic into what exists already just by telling him what I want. For example I want to do top down commanding where I select groups of soldiers and can change there formation by drag and dropping. Claude would whip somthing up , ide test it and iterate on feel and design slowly until im cool with it

Now I have to use deepseek harness. Havent tested it much yet but is this what you do ? Ive seen its decent enough. Or any recommendations? I liek to keep it simple. 

Oh and I always compacted convo on claude when id reach 400k

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body:
Cool. And it doesnt annoy you to have to compile and reopen editor every time in Unreal? I put Unreal on standby because of this.

So my workflow is just OpenCode + Deepseek 4.1 for the hard tasks. For stuff that is not complex, medium complexity tasks, I use GLM that consumes less. Thats it. But as I said im doing a lot of stuff myself too.

Now I believe you wont have the power of claude. But for a game where you like to build slowly over days, and have 100% control over what its doing. I think DeepSeek is good.

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: A common way to reduce angle drift is to make a simple 3D proxy and render orthographic views from fixed angles, using generated art as a texture or reference rather than asking for separate directions. For a 2D pipeline, a canonical reference sheet plus fixed scale/palette and automated crop, alpha, and size checks can catch routine cleanup, leaving manual review for odd silhouettes. Your free-tier workflow sounds reasonable if the time spent correcting assets is still manageable.
